title: South Korea's Interior Ministry says government administrative email system was hacked; joint check planned
date_note: Date of the ministry's release; the ministry says it was notified of the hack on 9 November.
org: Ministry of the Interior and Safety / National Information Resources Service
summary: South Korea's Interior Ministry says related agencies told it on 9 November that the administrative email system run by the National Information Resources Service was hacked; about 300 accounts showed abnormal access. The attacker came through some local governments' weak networks and used a single sign-on flaw. It reported the leak to the privacy regulator, notified those affected, plans a check with NIS and KISA for leftover malware, and aims to find the cause by year-end.
plain: Hackers got into South Korean government work email accounts through a login flaw. The ministry says it has notified those affected and is investigating.
exec: Shows how a weak local network and shared single sign-on can expose a national government system.
action: General advice: review single sign-on and the links between partner or local networks and your email system; look for abnormal sign-ins.

sources.name: Ministry of the Interior and Safety (korea.kr)

validation.note: Only Byline Network (16 Nov) was read; it relays the ministry's statement. The ministry's own press release on korea.kr did not load (ECONNRESET) on repeated tries, so it is not counted as read. The attacker is not named.
